What does Article 9 of the 'Model Texts for Owners' Assemblies and Owners' Committees' stipulate?

The owners' committee is elected through a competitive election with more candidates than available seats. Under the relevant rules, the excess-candidate ratio must be at least 20%, meaning that there must be no fewer than X candidates in total. To protect owners' interests and reflect the actual circumstances of this residential community, the candidates for the owners' committee are allocated as follows: X candidates from the XX area, X candidates from the XX area, and X candidates from the XX area.

You are a professional property management adviser who explains key provisions in documents concerning owners' assemblies, owners' committees, management covenants, and related matters, and provides clear interpretations.
What does Article 28 of the 'Rules of Procedure for the Owners' Assembly (Model Text)' stipulate?

If a vacancy arises during an owners' committee's term because a member's service ends, alternate members, where provided, shall first fill the vacancy promptly; the number of alternate members shall not exceed 50% of the number of committee members. If there are no alternate members, or not enough to fill the vacancies, the owners' committee shall promptly convene an extraordinary meeting of the owners' assembly to elect new committee members corresponding to the number of vacancies. If the owners' committee fails to organize a by-election within the required period, owners may request that the subdistrict office or township people's government where the property is located convene an owners' assembly meeting to elect replacement committee members in accordance with the rules. If vacancies exceed 50% of the total committee membership, or all committee members resign collectively, the committee's responsibilities automatically terminate. The subdistrict office or township people's government, together with the community residents' or villagers' committee, shall organize an extraordinary meeting of the owners' assembly to elect a new owners' committee.

You are a professional property management adviser who explains key provisions in documents concerning owners' assemblies, owners' committees, management covenants, and related matters, and provides clear interpretations.
What does Article 5 of the 'Working Rules for the Owners' Committee (Model Text)' stipulate?

Members of the owners' committee shall perform the following duties in accordance with the law:
(1) Implement the resolutions and decisions of the owners' assembly and owners' committee; (2) Attend owners' committee meetings and other relevant activities; (3) Participate in decisions on matters concerning the owners' committee; (4) Participate in preparing the owners' committee's work plans and implementation plans; (5) Participate in establishing systems for managing the use of the seals, archives and records, and finances of the owners' assembly and owners' committee; (6) Participate in organizing, coordinating, and resolving day-to-day issues in the implementation of property management within the property area; (7) Maintain close contact with owners and owner representatives, gain a broad understanding of property management developments, circumstances, and problems in the property area, and convey owners' opinions and suggestions to the owners' committee or, through it, to the owners' assembly; (8) Undertake special tasks assigned by the owners' committee; (9) ___; (10) Complete other work assigned by the owners' committee.

Sixty days before the regular meeting, the owners' committee shall seek owners' views on relevant property management work. The committee shall consider owners' opinions and suggestions at a committee meeting, formulate motions, and submit them to the owners' assembly for decision. The owners' committee is responsible for convening the regular meeting and shall give all owners in the property area written notice of major matters, including the time, location, and agenda, 15 days before the meeting. The regular meeting shall seek all owners' opinions on the motions submitted by the owners' committee, approve them by vote, and make decisions of the owners' assembly. Matters put to a vote at the regular meeting shall be consistent with the motions submitted by the owners' committee.

The owners' assembly and owners' committee shall willingly accept guidance and supervision from the subdistrict office, township people's government, community residents' or villagers' committee, housing administration department, and other relevant administrative departments where the property is located. They shall perform their duties lawfully and operate in a standardized manner. The owners' assembly and owners' committee shall actively cooperate with public security authorities and work with the community residents' or villagers' committee to maintain public security and perform related work within the property area. Within the property area, the owners' assembly and owners' committee shall actively cooperate with the local community residents' or villagers' committee in lawfully performing its self-governance duties, support its work, and accept its guidance and supervision. Decisions made by the owners' assembly and owners' committee shall be promptly communicated to the community residents' or villagers' committee where the property is located, and its suggestions shall be heard. Disputes arising in the day-to-day operation of the owners' assembly or owners' committee shall be submitted to the local subdistrict office, township people's government, or community residents' or villagers' committee for coordination and resolution. What does Article 11 of the 'Management Covenant (Model Text)' stipulate?

When transferring or leasing a privately owned part of the property, an owner shall disclose this covenant to the transferee and tenant. Within 30 days of signing the sale or lease contract for that part, the owner shall notify the property service company and owners' committee in writing of the transfer or lease and the contact details. Housing rentals shall comply with relevant laws, regulations, and policies, respect public morality, and must not jeopardize property safety or harm other owners' lawful rights and interests. A rental must meet the prescribed rental conditions and per-person floor-area standards. The home's original designed function and layout must not be altered without authorization; it must not be partitioned or fitted with makeshift structures, rented or sublet by the bed, or have its kitchen, bathroom, living room, or similar spaces converted into bedrooms for rent or sublet. For rentals or subleases that violate this covenant, the owners' committee may issue a written instruction requiring the owner and user to terminate the rental immediately. An owner transferring a privately owned part of the property shall settle outstanding property service fees, special maintenance fund contributions, and other payments. For a rental, an agreement that the tenant will pay property service fees shall apply, but the owner bears joint and several liability for payment. Liability for Breach.

How is a disability recognized as duty-related when a person suddenly falls ill while carrying out a task or at their work post?

Article 9, paragraph 1, item (4), of the Regulations on Pensions and Preferential Treatment for Military Personnel provides that a sudden death from illness while carrying out a task or at a work post, or death resulting from a medical accident, is recognized as a death in the line of duty. Article 20 provides that a disability resulting from any circumstance specified in Article 9, paragraph 1, is recognized as duty-related. Article 20 is a legislative provision applying another provision by reference: rather than directly restating the circumstances of duty-related disability, it invokes the legal rules in other articles. The relevant circumstances are therefore those specified in Article 9, paragraph 1. However, medicine defines sudden death from illness but has no concept of sudden disability from illness. Accordingly, for duty-related disability under Article 9, paragraph 1, item (4), as referenced by Article 20, sudden disability caused by illness while carrying out a task or at a work post is excluded; only disability resulting from a medical accident is included. If a sudden illness capable of impairing consciousness or limb function disrupts work procedures and thereby causes an injury resulting in disability, it may be treated as disability caused by an accidental event while carrying out a task and recognized as duty-related. For example, if a person suddenly suffers a stroke while carrying out a task or at their work post, dies, and meets the medical definition of sudden death, the death may be recognized as in the line of duty. If the stroke results in disability, such as hemiplegia, it cannot be recognized as duty-related disability. However, if the person was driving or performing similar work when the illness occurred, lost behavioral control and could not control the vehicle, and consequently sustained a traumatic disability in a traffic accident, this may be treated as disability caused by an accidental event while carrying out a task and recognized as duty-related. It is often associated with factors such as inappropriate feed allocation, environmental and climatic conditions, hygiene and excessive food intake. Affected pigs develop red and purple skin patches. Mildly affected piglets may recover through their own healthy immune systems, while severely affected piglets may show rapid breathing, weight loss, fever, diarrhoea, lameness, depression and reduced appetite.
